messages.content: Go back to San Diego. I want the car question settled against what we are actually doing, but do not touch the American flights or the Mission Bay reservation.

I’ll leave American Q7N4PL and Mission Bay MBY-624817 unchanged. I have three beach days, one zoo day, and two outings away from Mission Bay. Which days are the longer outings, and are the remaining beach days at or near the resort?

Saturday is arrival and staying at the resort. Sunday is Mission Beach. Monday is the zoo. Tuesday is La Jolla and Torrey Pines. Wednesday is another resort and beach day. Thursday is Coronado plus Cabrillo. Friday is open but probably close to the hotel, then we leave Saturday.

That makes this an eight-day, seven-night stay from June 20 through June 27. A car would be useful Monday, Tuesday, and Thursday, while the other days can reasonably be handled on foot or with short local rides. I’ll compare a full-stay airport rental with airport rides plus a shorter local rental, including taxes, fees, and the resort’s parking charge.
Yes. Include the real pickup limitations too. A cheaper plan is not useful if we lose half a day getting the car.

The current full-stay option is a midsize SUV at the airport from noon June 20 to 11:00 a.m. June 27. The rental is $612.84 including airport concession charges, taxes, and fees. Mission Bay parking is $46 per night, so seven nights add $322. That structure is $934.84 before fuel.
And the split version?

The best split version uses an XL rideshare from SAN to the resort on arrival, another XL back to SAN on departure, and a three-day midsize SUV from a Mission Valley office Tuesday through Thursday. The rental is $286.41 complete. Three parking nights add $138. The two airport rides are currently estimated at $48-$62 each, and zoo rides are about $27-$35 each way. Using the midpoint estimates, that plan totals $578.41 before fuel and any surge pricing.
Why does the local rental start Tuesday if the zoo is Monday?

Because the local office is closed Sunday and opens Monday at 8:00 a.m. A Monday pickup would push the zoo arrival later and require either returning by 5:00 p.m. Wednesday or paying through Thursday to cover the Coronado and Cabrillo outing. Keeping it Tuesday through Thursday means using rides to the zoo Monday, but it preserves the zoo morning.
Can it be picked up Monday evening and returned Thursday evening?

No. That office’s counter closes at 5:00 p.m. Monday through Friday, and it does not offer after-hours pickup. A Monday 4:30 p.m. pickup through Thursday 4:30 p.m. is available at $381.76 including taxes and fees. Parking would be four nights, or $184. With airport rides, that version is about $675.76 before fuel and surge pricing. Thursday’s return would also constrain the Cabrillo and Coronado day.
So the headline savings are overstated once all of that is included.

They narrow, but remain meaningful. Against the $934.84 full-stay arrangement, the Tuesday-through-Thursday split saves about $356.43. The Monday-through-Thursday split saves about $259.08. Those estimates include rental taxes and fees, hotel parking, both airport rides, and zoo rides where needed; they exclude fuel and possible rideshare surges.
What about Owen and luggage? He is 12, and we will have three checked suitcases plus carry-ons.

At 12, a rental company child seat is not automatically required under California’s age-based rule, though he should use the vehicle belt in the rear seat and you can decide based on belt fit. The airport rides should be XL vehicles for three passengers and that luggage. The local rental counter does not provide a hotel shuttle, so one adult would need a roughly 15-minute ride each way to collect and return the SUV.
That extra ride to the counter is not in your total, is it?

Correct. Adding estimated $22 rides each way raises the Tuesday-through-Thursday split to about $622.41 and the Monday-through-Thursday split to about $719.76. The full-stay airport rental remains $934.84. The practical savings are therefore about $312.43 or $215.08, respectively.
Lay out the actual friction for the cheaper Tuesday plan, not just the dollars.

It requires an XL ride from the airport on arrival, two rides for the zoo Monday, a separate ride to the rental office Tuesday morning, counter processing during office hours, a Thursday return by 5:00 p.m., a ride back to the resort after return, and another XL ride to the airport Saturday. It also means unloading beach gear and personal items before Thursday’s return. The full-stay rental is collected once at SAN, remains available for every outing and the open Friday, and is returned at the airport before the flight.
Check the full-week car one more time. Same category and total, and make sure the return time fits the flight. Do not substitute a prepaid rate.

I rechecked it. The pay-later midsize SUV is still available at $612.84 complete from noon June 20 through 11:00 a.m. June 27, with cancellation allowed until pickup. The airport location is open for both times, and the return leaves the existing flight schedule intact. Seven nights of resort parking remain $322, making local transportation $934.84 before fuel.
Use that as the plan. It costs more, but it is the practical choice for this itinerary. What does that make the whole San Diego trip?

The confirmed flights and hotel total $5,737.92. Adding the full-stay rental and seven nights of parking brings the complete planned trip cost to $6,672.76 before fuel. The rental itself is still only selected, not booked; American Q7N4PL and Mission Bay MBY-624817 remain unchanged.
Book the pay-later SUV at that price. Nothing else changes.

The midsize SUV is confirmed for noon June 20 through 11:00 a.m. June 27 at $612.84 including taxes and airport fees. Confirmation is A6R29481, pay later, cancellable until pickup. With $322 in resort parking, transportation is $934.84 before fuel and the full San Diego trip is $6,672.76 before fuel. The American flights and Mission Bay reservation were not changed.
